references.text: The psalmist prays: 'Teach me your way, Lord! I will walk in your truth.' To 'do the truth' in John 3:21 has a close parallel to walking in the truth, which involves a lifestyle rooted in God's will. See Psalm 86:11.

The prophet Isaiah points out that God's works are accomplished through his people: 'All that we have achieved, you have done for us.' This reflects the idea in John 3:21 that deeds are done 'in God'. See Isaiah 26:12.
Jesus is the true light coming into the world. In John 3:21, whoever does the truth comes to the light—the same light described in John 1:9 as enlightening every person.

The immediate context explains that the light has come into the world, but people loved darkness more than light because their deeds were evil. Whoever does evil hates the light. John 3:21 is the positive counterpart to this. See John 3:19-20.

Paul urges believers to walk as children of light and bear the fruit of light, which is goodness, righteousness, and truth, and to expose the deeds of darkness. This expands on the theme in John 3:21 about coming to the light so that deeds may be made visible. See Ephesians 5:8-11.

John writes that if we say we have fellowship with God yet walk in darkness, we lie and do not do the truth. But if we walk in the light, we have fellowship with one another. The expression 'doing the truth' (ποιῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν) is the same in John 3:21 and 1 John 1:6.

Jesus says that whoever remains in him bears much fruit, for apart from him we can do nothing. The idea that deeds are 'done in God' (ἐν θεῷ ἐστιν εἰργασμένα) in John 3:21 points to the same truth: good works spring from fellowship with God. See John 15:4-5.

Paul writes that the Lord will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and reveal the motives of hearts. This reflects the motif in John 3:21 that the righteous come to the light so that their deeds may be made visible. See 1 Corinthians 4:5.
Paul writes that it is God who works in believers, both to will and to act. This aligns with John 3:21, where deeds are 'done in God'—God is the source of good works. See Philippians 2:13.

Jesus says: 'I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness but will have the light of life.' Coming to the light in John 3:21 means coming to Jesus himself, who here identifies as the light of the world. See John 8:12.
